headline: Dhaka outraged over India allowing Hasina's media event in New Delhi
summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs calls the interaction 'detrimental' to resetting bilateral ties and an affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh.
details: The Bangladesh government has expressed deep outrage after India allowed ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina to interact with the media in New Delhi.
In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs described the event as 'deeply hurtful' to Bangladeshis and detrimental to the development of harmonious ties between the two nations.
Dhaka stated that the interaction occurred on the second anniversary of the July Revolution, calling it an affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh and an insult to the martyrs of the uprising.

The foreign ministry accused Hasina of using the platform to launch 'venomous vitriol' against the state and its people, while denying UN findings on civilian killings during the July-August 2024 uprising.
Dhaka expressed regret that India permitted the event despite concerns conveyed beforehand regarding its potential ramifications on bilateral relations.
The government also noted that repeated requests for Hasina's return under the 2013 Bangladesh-India Extradition Treaty have yet to receive a response from New Delhi.

During the media interaction hosted by the Foreign Correspondents' Club of South Asia, Hasina called for the lifting of the ban on the Awami League and stated she would return to Bangladesh in December.
caption:
Bangladesh is outraged. India allowing Sheikh Hasina to speak to the media in New Delhi is called 'detrimental' to bilateral ties.

The Bangladesh government has expressed deep outrage after India allowed ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina to interact with the media in New Delhi.

In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs described the event as 'deeply hurtful' to Bangladeshis and detrimental to the development of harmonious ties between the two nations.

Dhaka stated that the interaction occurred on the second anniversary of the July Revolution, calling it an affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh and an insult to the martyrs of the uprising.

The foreign ministry accused Hasina of using the platform to launch 'venomous vitriol' against the state and its people, while denying UN findings on civilian killings during the July-August 2024 uprising.

Dhaka expressed regret that India permitted the event despite concerns conveyed beforehand regarding its potential ramifications on bilateral relations.

The government also noted that repeated requests for Hasina's return under the 2013 Bangladesh-India Extradition Treaty have yet to receive a response from New Delhi.

During the media interaction hosted by the Foreign Correspondents' Club of South Asia, Hasina called for the lifting of the ban on the Awami League and stated she would return to Bangladesh in December.

headline: Planned outages: 4-hour power cuts scheduled for Thursday
summary: Several areas across the country will face electricity outages for maintenance work on Thursday.
details: Several regions across Bangladesh will experience planned power outages on Thursday.
The outages are scheduled to last for up to four hours in the affected areas.
These power cuts are typically carried out for essential maintenance and system upgrades to the grid.
Residents in the affected zones are advised to plan their activities accordingly to avoid inconvenience.
